title: Check for a Misroute
subtitle: Assigned category vs worked category
scenario: The learning step: compare the category a ticket was assigned to the category it was actually worked as. A mismatch is a misroute - the signal that tunes the taxonomy. TKT-4001 was assigned outage and worked as outage, so it is clean.
input: TKT-4001 was assigned category outage at classification, and the resolution record shows it was worked as outage. Compare them: same category means not misrouted. Record the assigned and worked categories and the misrouted flag.
instructions: Record the assigned and worked categories.
Set misrouted false when they match (they do here).
Return one valid JSON object, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Build one JSON misroute check for TKT-4001: assignedCategory outage, workedCategory outage, misrouted false (they match).
successMessage: No misroute. Assigned and worked categories match - a clean route.
editorHelper: Same category = not misrouted; a mismatch is the signal.

intro.heading: The signal that tunes the taxonomy

sections.title: A misroute is data, not blame
sections.body: Comparing assigned to worked is not about catching an agent - it is about catching a category that misleads. A misroute is a fact the taxonomy loop learns from.

sections.title: Match here, mismatch elsewhere
sections.body: TKT-4001 matched, so it is clean. The check earns its keep on the days it does not match - a ticket assigned billing but worked as a bug points at a confusing category.

sections.title: One flag, big leverage
sections.body: A single misrouted flag per ticket, totaled over a day, is what tells Support Ops which categories to split or clarify. Small signal, systemic fix.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A misroute check the digest counts and the taxonomy feedback loop reads.

fieldGuide.meaning: The category it was actually worked as.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd compare what a ticket was filed under to what it turned out to be, and note the mismatches for review.

takeaway.heading: Misroute checked
points: You compared the assigned and worked categories.
They matched, so TKT-4001 is not a misroute.
A misroute is data that points at a confusing category, not blame.
The digest counts this and the taxonomy loop reads it.
The workflow can now catch misroutes that tune the taxonomy.
